title: A methanogen hydrolase reveals the structure of archaeal peptidoglycan.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC metadata (closed access, no PMCID, hasSuppl=N, no text-mined accessions); Crossref record; NCBI elink from PMID 42778595 (no GEO/SRA/BioProject links); PDBe text search (no structure from this work; only older pseudomurein ligase/endoisopeptidase entries 6vr7/6vr8/7ufp/8z4h/8z4n); Zenodo search (nothing); PRIDE project PXD052257 metadata and full file list (11 files, 10.51 GB: ten Thermo .raw files of 1.0-1.3 GB each, one 370.5 MB MaxQuant 'txt.zip', one 0.86 MB FASTA). I downloaded and parsed the FASTA: 1,783 sequences, which is simply the UniProt reference proteome UP000001992 for Methanobrevibacter smithii ATCC 35061, not data the paper generated.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the science: the new sugar N-acetylarmosamine, the alternating beta(1,4)/beta(1,3) glycan linkages, ArmA's dual glycosidase plus peptidase activity, the phylogenetic claim that ArmA homologues are restricted to peptidoglycan-bearing archaea, and the cytokinesis requirement. All of this is in the abstract only; the full text, methods, data availability statement and supplementary tables are behind the Nature paywall with no PubMed Central copy, so I could not read them.

a1_downloadable.note: PRIDE PXD052257 is public under CC0 and downloads without login (I pulled the 0.86 MB FASTA and got HTTP 200 plus a 370,529,200-byte content length on txt.zip). But it is the only dataset I could find for this paper, and nine of its eleven files are raw mass spectrometry, which project policy forbids downloading.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAILS. Nothing in the deposited data is a prediction target. The MaxQuant output is a protein-identification/intensity table for ten mass-spec runs of one organism; the paper's actual findings (a chemical structure, an enzyme activity, a homologue distribution across archaeal genomes) are figures and supplementary tables, not a label column. Any machine-learning target here - for example 'does this archaeon make pseudomurein-type cell wall' - would have to be constructed by joining the paper's homologue list to genome annotations and taxonomy, and that homologue list sits in paywalled supplementary tables I could not retrieve.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein sequences are present (1,783 sequences in the UniProt proteome FASTA I opened), so inputs would not need resolving - but they are generic UniProt entries, not paper-specific measurements.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessable in any useful way: the only quantitative file is a MaxQuant search output (arbitrary intensity/LFQ units) and I could not open it under the 50 MB cap. No units table, because there is no measurement table.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS on the real unit of analysis. The deposit holds 10 mass-spectrometry runs of a single organism (Methanobrevibacter smithii ATCC 35061). The structural result is one glycan architecture; the enzyme result is one enzyme tested on a handful of methanogens. Far under the ~400-1,500 labelled rows the checklist requires.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.86 MB FASTA opened; 370 MB MaxQuant archive not opened (over the 50 MB cap); 10.1 GB of raw spectra deliberately not downloaded.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here - the absence of a modelling table is.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked. The paper's full text and supplementary tables are not retrievable (closed access, no PubMed Central record), so there is no paper-stated count to compare the PRIDE file list against. Note also that the PRIDE deposit still describes the enzyme under its earlier name 'TalA' and the sugar as talosaminuronic acid, while the published paper renames the enzyme 'ArmA' and the sugar 'N-acetylarmosamine' - the deposit metadata and the paper are out of step.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists, so provenance cannot be traced. The nearest candidate label - 'this genome has archaeal peptidoglycan' - would come from the authors' own HMM (hidden Markov model) homology search plus taxonomy, i.e. a bioinformatic call rather than a physical measurement, which is exactly the circularity A8 warns about.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) would be the natural backbone for any enzyme-function version of this project
backbone.hardware: CPU would suffice for 1,783 sequences, but there is nothing to train a head on
backbone.licence: ESM-2 weights are MIT-licensed; the PRIDE deposit is CC0

integration.partner_dataset: CAZy / Pfam-InterPro (enzyme family assignments) plus GTDB archaeal genomes, joinable on UniProt accession and taxonomy ID
integration.join_key: UniProt accession (present in the FASTA headers I read) and NCBI taxonomy ID 420247
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which archaeal genomes encode a pseudomurein-type cell wall, and can that be called from sequence alone? - a real question, but this paper's deposit supplies none of the labelled examples needed to answer it.

controls.positive_control: None available: with ten mass-spec runs of one organism there is no held-out signal a model could be asked to recover.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless without labels.
controls.external_validation: The 2024 pangenomics study of archaeal pseudomurein biosynthesis genes (mSystems, doi:10.1128/msystems.01401-24) would be the external source for a genome-level cell-wall-type project, but it is a separate dataset, not this paper's.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim can be made from this paper's deposited data, because the deposit contains only raw proteomics spectra from one organism and a copy of a public reference proteome - there is no measured quantity varying across enough examples to predict.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an archaeal protein's sequence to predict whether its organism builds a pseudomurein cell wall.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on archaeal genomes labelled by whether they encode the pseudomurein cell-wall machinery, using protein sequences as input. The number of labelled genomes this paper supplies is unknown to me, because the homologue tables are in paywalled supplementary material.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be a yes/no cell-wall-type call per genome. The true answer would come from the authors' homology search plus a handful of wet-lab enzyme-activity tests on diverse methanogens, not from a direct measurement on each genome.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Microbial-ecology and gut-microbiome groups would like to know which archaea have a drug-targetable cell wall; but as framed the label is itself a sequence-search result, so a model would mostly be relearning the search.

ml_idea: No viable machine-learning project. The only idea the data suggests - classifying archaeal genomes by cell-wall type from sequence - has its labels generated by homology search (so it is circular), and the labelled list is locked in paywalled supplementary tables.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: 1,783 protein sequences through a small ESM-2 checkpoint on CPU is well under an hour, and the FASTA parsed in under a second. Cross-validation time is null because there is no label set to cross-validate.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: List the files in PRIDE PXD052257 and count the quantitative rows: ten .raw files from one organism plus a public reference proteome means no feature/label table exists. That one API call, which I made, kills the project.

verdict_reason: This is a beautiful structural-biochemistry paper with no modelling dataset attached. Part A2 fails (no prediction target is a column anywhere), A5 fails (ten mass-spec runs of a single organism), and A7/A8 are unverifiable because the paper is closed access with no PubMed Central copy, so the supplementary tables holding the phylogenetic homologue list cannot be read. The only openly downloadable artefacts are 10.1 GB of raw Thermo spectra (which policy forbids downloading), a 370 MB MaxQuant search archive over the size cap, and a 0.86 MB copy of the public UniProt proteome for Methanobrevibacter smithii that the paper did not generate.
